posts.text: 🇪🇺 Kaja Kallas's job as EU foreign policy chief is starting to look shaky. EU leaders left her off Europe's Ukraine peace talks team after she had openly pitched herself as the envoy. Germany has proposed putting her under Ursula von der Leyen's supervision, which would effectively turn the EU's top diplomat into a Commission staffer. Von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa were asked about her and didn't say a word in her defence. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni reportedly told leaders behind closed doors that Kallas doesn't have the weight for serious negotiations. The complaints from diplomats are piling up. They say she goes off script on China and Israel and launches initiatives without asking member states, like the defence expert group that had to be scrapped in September. They also say she spent months opposing any talks with Russia, then asked to lead them. Her pitch in Dublin, "Russians don't want me," was called "clumsy." One diplomat reminded her that the job is finding the lowest common denominator among 27 capitals, not freelancing. Some commentators say the post itself is weak, because EU treaties give the foreign policy chief very little real power. But Kallas has an extra problem: neither the Commission nor the member states are backing her. She still has fans, but mostly outside Brussels, among people who like her hard line on Russia. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

Во львовском "Эпицентре" ввели ограничения на продажу бананов — подсолнечного масла "Риднокрай". Теперь полагается не более 2-х бутылок в одном чеке, сообщают СМИ. После ударов ВС РФ по ряду предприятий, производящих подсолнечное масло, аборигены Львова и области зачастили в магазины, намереваясь запастись маслом впрок. Их не остановил комментарий министра агрополитики Украины Высоцкого о том, что дефицит этого продукта не прогнозируется. Здесь знают, что власти умеют хорошо врать, доверие к ним — ниже статистической погрешности. Поэтому в скупке ряда продуктов и предметов первой необходимости наблюдается ажиотаж. 📆 On November 17, the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) marked the 60th anniversary. In 1966, on the initiative of the Soviet Union, UNIDO was established as an autonomous organisation within the #UN , and in 1985, thanks to the efforts of the USSR, it was granted the status of a UN specialised agency. ☝️ Over the past six decades, the Organisation has promoted inclusive and sustainable industrial development across its member states , particularly in Africa, strengthening their productive capacities and integration into the global economy. As a global forum, it facilitates international dialogue on promoting industrialisation, bringing together representatives of the public and private sectors alongside non-governmental and academic organisations. 🤝 The Russian Federation is a long-standing and reliable partner of the Organisation. As an active participant and key donor to international efforts in sustainable industrial development, Russia attaches particular importance to multilateral cooperation within the relevant bodies of the UN system. During the forthcoming 54th session of the Industrial Development Board , scheduled for November 23–25, a number of commemorative events are scheduled to mark the Organisation’s anniversary, including a thematic seminar entitled “Russia and UNIDO: 60 Years Together” .

🎙 Opening remarks by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at the meeting with Prime Minister of Thailand Anutin Charnvirakul on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Summit (Shenzhen, November 18, 2026) 💬 Vladimir Putin: I am pleased to see you again . We last met at the Russia-ASEAN Summit in Kazan in June. 🇷🇺 🇹🇭 Thailand is a longstanding partner of Russia. Next year marks the 130th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between our countries. We are committed to further developing our wide-ranging bilateral ties . Our governments, parliaments and foreign ministries maintain active contacts . Bilateral trade is growing . In 2025, trade rose by 2.3% . In January-August 2026 , it grew by 37.4% compared with the same period last year. This is a good result. There is considerable scope for mutually beneficial cooperation in energy, transport, logistics, agribusiness and investment. The Joint Commission on Bilateral Cooperation is tasked with advancing work in these areas. Our cultural and people-to-people ties are also growing . Thailand successfully hosted a series of events this year as part of the Russian Seasons festival . Education has traditionally been an important part of our cooperation . Thailand has been allocated 50 government scholarships for the 2026–2027 academic year, and around 109 Thai students are currently studying in Russia. 🏝 Thailand is a very popular destination for Russian tourists . Nearly 2 million Russians visited Thailand as tourists in 2025. In the first nine months of 2026, 1.3 million did so. Our representatives coordinate their efforts in various international and regional forums . We cooperate constructively within #APEC and through the #RussiaASEAN Dialogue Partnership. Mr Prime Minister, we welcome Thailand’s participation in #BRICS as a partner country since 2025. 🤝 Our relations are developing across a wide range of areas. I look forward to discussing with you and your colleagues how we can build on what we have achieved so far and what steps we will take together in the near future. #RussiaThailand
